title: docs(core): repair both `registerPlugin` examples in PHASE2_IMPLEMENTATION.md
body:
Fixes #18000

Clause-②: no

Both `registerPlugin` examples in `packages/core/PHASE2_IMPLEMENTATION.md` failed when
copied verbatim: seven keys across them are spellings that `@objectstack/spec` and
`@objectstack/core` both refuse today. Every replacement spelling comes from the key's own
`retiredKey()` prescription — none was invented, and no key was deleted to make a block parse.

## What changed (line numbers on the dispatch base `d93400f42e`)

| line | was | now | why |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 31 | `interval: 30000` | `intervalMs: 30000` | renamed in `@objectstack/spec` 17 (#17780) |
| 32 | `timeout: 5000` | `timeoutMs: 5000` | renamed in `@objectstack/spec` 17 (#17780) |
| 35 | `autoRestart: true` | deleted | removed in 18 (#12032, ADR-0049) — nothing ever restarted a plugin |
| 36 | `maxRestartAttempts: 3` | deleted | removed in 18 (#12032) — it capped a restart that never happened |
| 37 | `restartBackoff: 'exponential'` | deleted | removed in 18 (#12032) — it delayed a restart that never happened |
| 70 | `watchPatterns` | deleted | removed in 18 (#12428, ADR-0049) — no watcher was ever constructed |
| 71 | `debounceDelay: 1000` | `debounceDelayMs: 1000` | renamed in `@objectstack/spec` 17 (#17780) |

Each deletion is followed by the affordance its own prescription names, so the block still
answers the question the deleted key was asked: poll `getHealthStatus()` / `getHealthReport()`
for the restart trio (the monitor reports, it does not act), and run your own watcher and call
`hotReload.scheduleReload('my-plugin', reloadFn)` for `watchPatterns`.

## Verification

**R1 — re-taken on the dispatch base, not inherited.** `git grep -c` per key against that one
file at `d93400f42e`: `autoRestart` 1 · `maxRestartAttempts` 1 · `restartBackoff` 1 ·
`watchPatterns` 1 · `interval` 3 · `timeout` 2 · `debounceDelay` 1 — identical to the dispatch's
reading. Dark control: a fabricated key returns 0 in the same file with the same instrument.

**R2 — resolved by occurrence, not by count.** `interval` 3 = prose `:16`
("Configurable health check intervals"), the example `:31`, prose `:348`. `timeout` 2 = the
example `:32`, prose `:56` ("Graceful shutdown with configurable timeout") — `shutdownTimeout`
does not match the lower-case spelling, which is why the count is 2 and not 3. Only `:31` and
`:32` were retired-key occurrences; the three prose lines are untouched. ⚠️ The same bare counts
survive this fix for a *different* reason — `intervalMs` / `debounceDelayMs` contain the old
words as substrings, and the three deleted keys are now named in the replacement comments — so
after this PR a bare count is still not a verdict. The verdict instrument is key POSITION inside
a fenced block: retired keys in key position, before 7, after 0.

**R3 — measured per key; the dispatch had not verified it.** One-shot probe (throwaway, not
committed) against both refusal channels: the spec tombstone (`PluginHealthCheckSchema` /
`HotReloadConfigSchema` `safeParse`) and the `@objectstack/core` runtime door
(`PluginHealthMonitor.registerPlugin` / `HotReloadManager.registerPlugin`, which call
`assertNoRetiredKeys` before storing anything).

| key | spec refuses | core refuses | prescription carried |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `interval` | yes | yes | rename to `intervalMs` |
| `timeout` | yes | yes | rename to `timeoutMs` |
| `autoRestart` | yes | yes | delete the key |
| `maxRestartAttempts` | yes | yes | delete the key |
| `restartBackoff` | yes | yes | delete the key |
| `watchPatterns` | yes | yes | delete the key |
| `debounceDelay` | yes | yes | rename to `debounceDelayMs` |
| `fabricatedDarkControlKey` (dark control) | **no** | **no** | — |

So all seven are genuinely retired, none is merely "accepted and ignored", and the instrument
discriminates. Whole-block readings: the health block as it stood refuses first at `autoRestart`
(`[HealthMonitor] Plugin 'my-plugin': 'autoRestart' was removed from PluginHealthCheck in
@objectstack/spec 18 …`), the hot-reload block refuses first at `watchPatterns`; **both repaired
blocks parse clean and register clean on both channels**.

An earlier run of that probe reported `core.refused=true` for *every* case including the dark
control — a stub logger with no `child()`. The dark control is what caught it; the readings above
are from the corrected run.

## Gates

> **Corrected after review** (os-dev seat, `session_01CqmCgU5RGDoJYhHUMVp2af`). This section first
> read **35 run / 4 NOT MEASURED**. That was a real reading, but of the EARLIER of two runs of the
> same 39 commands — the one taken at `e7da59e475` before a build existed. The reading for the head
> this PR points at is **37 run / 2 NOT MEASURED**, which is what the report comment on #18000
> carries. Numbers below corrected from the recorded exit codes; the cause is stated rather than
> patched over, because it decides whether the count is stable (it is not — it is a function of
> build state).

Derived at this head from the real changed path, then reconciled:
`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` ⇒ 39 families;
`--ran` with a recorded exit code per line ⇒ **39 derived, 37 run, 2 NOT MEASURED, 0 UNRUN**
(derivation taken from tree `45caf2a451`). Every exit code was written to disk before anything was
read, one file per command.

NOT MEASURED (both exited **3**, the prerequisite-refusal code, not a finding):
`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:lean-entry-closure` — both LOAD built entry points for
every package that declares an exports map, so the three-package closure build in this worktree
was not enough to satisfy them. A markdown file that no build reads and no `files[]` ships cannot
move them; CI runs them on a fully built tree.

**Why the two runs disagree, in one mechanism.** Between them I ran
`pnpm --filter '@objectstack/core^...' build`, which created `dist/` for exactly three packages
(`spec`, `types`, `metadata-core`). Three families read the filesystem rather than the diff and
flipped with it, none of them because of anything in this PR:

| family | run 1 (`e7da59e475`, nothing built) | run 2 (`45caf2a451`, 3 packages built) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `check:dts-closure` | exit 3 — PREREQUISITE NOT MET, no package has a `dist/` | exit 0 — "3 built package(s) swept — 39/39 declared declaration file(s) present" |
| `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content` | exit 3 — same refusal | exit 0 — "3 built package(s) swept — 52 map(s), none embed source text" |
| `check:cross-package-test-inputs` | exit 0 | exit 1 — names `packages/cli/test/init-created-files-summary.e2e.test.ts` walking into `packages/spec/dist/`, a radius no declared glob reaches |

The first two are recorded as **run** above because on this head they were measured. The third is
recorded as **exit 0**, the verdict in the tree state CI runs it in: `lint.yml`'s "Cross-package
test inputs" step has no build ahead of it. Two-leg proof that build state is the whole cause —
parking `packages/spec/dist` away and re-running gives exit 0 ("29 package(s) read outside
themselves, all declared"); restoring it was verified by file count (216 = 216) and a clean
`git status`. That blind spot — a gate that can only SEE the undeclared walk radius in a built
tree, run by CI in an unbuilt one — is handed to the PM as a finding of its own, not repaired here.

⚠️ So neither count is meaningful without its tree state: in CI's unbuilt lint job those first two
families will refuse with exit 3 again, exactly as run 1 recorded. What is stable is that no
family's verdict moves with this diff.

Package-scoped, after `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/core^...' build` (the closure build the first
test run turned out to need — it failed on `Cannot find package '@objectstack/spec/system'`,
a prerequisite miss, not a red):

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core test` — **51 files / 1316 tests passed**, exit 0
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core typecheck` — exit 0 (`tsc --noEmit`, the examples project, and
  `check:test-typecheck`)

No test in the tree reads this document: `git grep` for `PHASE2_IMPLEMENTATION` outside the file
itself returns five hits, all of them comments. Repo-wide scans (`pnpm lint` and the rest) are
CI's.

## Changeset: none, deliberately

`packages/core/package.json` `files` is `['dist', 'README.md', 'CHANGELOG.md']`, and
`packages/core/tsup.config.ts` builds only `src/index.ts` and `src/logger.ts` — no step copies
markdown into `dist/`. So this document reaches contributors reading the repo and never an
installer: nothing published moves, which is the `skip-changeset` criterion. Positive control on
the instrument: `README.md` **is** in that `files` list, so the list does discriminate.
`Clause-②: no` — no authorable surface widens or narrows here.

## Acceptance notes

Everything below was found by the whole-file sweep the card asked for, measured, and
**deliberately left out of this diff** under the dispatch's edit boundary (fix what is stale for
the same reason — a retired spelling inside a copy-pasteable example; anything stale for another
reason is reported, not edited).

**1. #16208 — its two sites are NOT in this file, and one of them is already repaired.** The
dispatch describes #16208 as an open, held card "against sections 4 and 5 of this same document".
Measured at `d93400f42e`: the two sites #16208's own body names are in *other* files, and this
document is only their SUBJECT.

- `packages/core/PHASE2_IMPLEMENTATION.md` contains **zero** occurrences of `core/security`.
  Sections 4 and 5 import from the root barrel (`import { PluginPermissionManager } from
  '@objectstack/core';` at `:161`, `import { PluginSandboxRuntime } from '@objectstack/core';`
  at `:219`) — PR #16205's repair, still in place.
- Site 1, `docs/qa/platform-checklist/FOLLOW-UPS.md:196-205`: **already repaired**. It now reads
  "What SURVIVED that removal in the same document, **and how it was closed**" and describes the
  subpath teaching in the past tense, naming #15931 and PR #16205.
- Site 2, `packages/core/src/security/security-scanner-retirement.pin.test.ts:46-48`: **still
  stale**. The header comment still says "`PHASE2_IMPLEMENTATION.md` sections 4 and 5 still teach
  it" — false at this base, by the first bullet.

So this PR touches no line #16208 owns, there is no edit conflict between the two cards, and
#16208 is now a one-file, one-comment card. Its state is the PM's call, not this seat's. Its
restart condition (any commit touching that pin test file since `5abca1792e`) was NOT evaluated
here: this checkout is shallow, and a windowed history answer from a truncated history is exactly
the false reading that condition must not be decided on.

**2. `blockedHosts` at `:235` (`:241` after this diff) — different class, left in place.** The
sandbox example writes `blockedHosts: ['malicious.com']`. `SandboxConfigSchema`
(`packages/spec/src/kernel/plugin-security-advanced.zod.ts:390-396`) declares `deniedHosts`, and
`packages/core/src/security/sandbox-runtime.ts:261` reads `config.network.deniedHosts`. This is
**not** a retired spelling — there is no tombstone, and `blockedHosts` occurs exactly once in the
entire repository, in this document. Measured consequence: `safeParse` **succeeds** and the key is
silently dropped (parsed network keys come back as `mode`, `allowedHosts`, `maxConnections`; no
`deniedHosts` appears). A reader copying that block gets a sandbox that does not block the host it
names — a silent strip, not the loud refusal the seven keys give. TypeScript catches it as an
excess property; anything that reaches the parse does not. **Recommend filing** (class (a): the
example fails when copied, with a named repro) — one-word repair, `blockedHosts` ⇒ `deniedHosts`.
Dedupe words: `blockedHosts`, `deniedHosts`, `SandboxConfigSchema`, `PHASE2_IMPLEMENTATION`,
`sandbox example`.

**3. `kernel.logger` at `:319-323` (`:325-329` after this diff) — different class, left in
place.** The Integration block does `new PluginHealthMonitor(kernel.logger)` for five classes.
`ObjectKernel` declares `private logger: ObjectLogger` (`packages/core/src/kernel.ts:107`) and
`ObjectKernelBase` declares `protected logger: Logger`
(`packages/core/src/kernel-base.ts:36`) — no public getter. Copying that block into TypeScript
does not compile. Not a key spelling and not a retired key, so out of this diff's boundary.
Dedupe words: `kernel.logger`, `private logger`, `ObjectKernel`, `Integration with Kernel`,
`PHASE2_IMPLEMENTATION`.

**4. Two prose claims falsified by the same #12032 retirement — left in place, and the tension is
deliberate.** `:13` ("real-time health checking and **auto-recovery**") and `:18`
("**Auto-restart** with backoff strategies (fixed, linear, exponential)") advertise the capability
whose three keys this PR deletes. They are true of no runtime:
`packages/core/src/health-monitor.ts` states "It REPORTS; it does not act on what it finds", and
the tombstone records that `attemptRestart` called `destroy()` and stopped. They are prose, not a
retired spelling inside an example, so the boundary keeps them out of this diff — which does leave
the document advertising at `:18` a capability its example no longer configures. Flagged rather
than smuggled: this is Prime Directive #10's "advertise a capability the runtime doesn't deliver",
worth a card of its own. Dedupe words: `auto-recovery`, `Auto-restart with backoff`,
`PHASE2_IMPLEMENTATION`, `#12032`, `health monitor features`.

**5. Observations, not filings.** `:373` links `[MICROKERNEL_IMPROVEMENT_PLAN.md](../../MICROKERNEL_IMPROVEMENT_PLAN.md)`
and no such file exists at the repo root (`ARCHITECTURE.md`, the sibling link, does). `:343` says
to run tests with `npm test` in a pnpm workspace. `:55` lists "File watching integration points"
as a hot-reload feature, which after #12428 is true only of `scheduleReload`.

**6. Same-name tombstones on other defs are NOT defects here.** Cross-checking every key in every
fenced block against the spelling KEY-colon-`retiredKey(` repo-wide turns up `enabled`, `actions`, `fields`,
`mode`, and `interval` / `timeout` again — all on unrelated schemas (`metadata-loader.zod.ts`,
`manifest.zod.ts`, `ui/component.zod.ts`, `api/router.zod.ts`, …). The keys in this document are
judged against the def they are actually passed to, so those collisions are noise. Within the four
schemas these examples really use, the tombstoned set is exactly the seven repaired above.
